source.filter_text: acq_date (UTC) from 2023-08-01 to 2023-10-31 inclusive; longitude 110.7 to 115.9 and latitude -3.6 to 0.9 (a bounding box around Central Kalimantan, NOT the province polygon: it also takes in edges of West, South and East Kalimantan); type == 0 (presumed vegetation fire); confidence in {n, h, nominal, high} (low dropped). lon/lat rounded to 3 decimals, frp (MW) to 1 decimal; isNight = 1 when daynight == "N".
source.product: VIIRS S-NPP 375 m (NASA FIRMS, standard processing)
source.day_is: FIRMS acq_date in UTC (one frame = one acq_date)

bbox_note: Bounding box around Central Kalimantan (Kalteng), not the province polygon.
reappear_rule: A point on day t is "re-appeared after a gap" when the most recent earlier point within 0.03 degrees (plain Euclidean distance in lon/lat degrees, about 3.3 km) was seen 3 to 14 days before t. That means (a) a point within 0.03 degrees existed 3 to 14 days earlier, and (b) on the days in between (at least the 2 consecutive days right before t) no point existed within 0.03 degrees. Only days inside this file are looked at (nothing before 2023-08-01), so the first possible re-appearance is on 2023-08-04. Stored per day in "re" as indices into that day's "pts". It says the record had a gap there, not why (smoke, cloud, a missed pass or a fire that went out and restarted are all possible).
